Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: The direct case marks S and P in the imperfective aspect and operates as the absolutive. The oblique case marks the ergative in that context. There are different forms of the pronoun for the direct and oblique cases.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: Verified against Bashir & Conners 2019:443 (ex. 9.78) and p.196. Value 0 confirmed. In the perfective transitive the 1st person subject stays in the DIRECT case, identical to S (mae~ do amb kha-de '1SG.DIR ate two mangoes'). The grammar states explicitly (p.196) that 1st/2nd person subjects remain in the direct case form. A = S = direct: no ergative flagging.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Verified against Bashir & Conners 2019:443 (ex. 9.79). Value 0 confirmed. 2nd person subject stays in DIRECT case in the perfective transitive (tuu~ ki kita e '2SG.DIR what done'). No ergative flagging on 2nd person pronouns.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: Value 1 confirmed, but cited evidence refined. The 3rd person PRONOUN shows ergative alignment: ex. 6.3, p.196 (o ne gaddi ... litti '3SG.ERG rented a cart'); Table 6.3, pp.194-195 contrasts direct o/e vs. oblique os/aes. NB: the originally cited ex. 9.80 (p.443) is a full NP (hukam), not a pronoun. /ne/ is optional in Lahore Panjabi, but the 3rd person A is in the OBLIQUE (distinct from direct S) with or without /ne/, so ergative alignment holds either way.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Verified against Bashir & Conners 2019:443 (ex. 9.80; also ex. 9.82). Value 1 confirmed. Full-NP A takes oblique + ergative /ne/ in the perfective (hukam ne ... ditta 'the officials (ERG) ordered'; dade ne thukkiya 'grandfather (ERG) spat'), distinct from the direct case of S.
